Resolves #20081

Ties the lifetime of a plugin-installed tab header title cap (`maxWidth` + `neo-tab-overflow-capped`) to the strip's usable room across both focus-gated action-rail transitions and cross-toolbar tab moves:

1. **Focus-gated rail transitions (`src/toolbar/Base.mjs`, `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`):** `Toolbar#applyContextualActionState` now fires `actionGeometryChange` (`{contextual: true}`) after committing a non-silent VDom update, and `Overflow#onActionGeometryChange` re-projects (`this.project(false)`) unless the owner uses hover-reveal reservation (`showOnHover === true`, preserving `#20011`).
2. **Cross-toolbar cap provenance & bounded drag-freeze guard (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`):** `Overflow.buttonCaps` (a static `WeakMap` keyed by the button instance) records `{cap, plugin}` alongside the plugin's `appliedCaps` / `appliedCapButtons` Maps, `Overflow#releaseDepartedCap` shares one ownership guard between `applySplit` and `destroy` so a retiring plugin never strips the cap or ellipsis class from a button now owned by another live `Overflow` strip, and `Overflow#project` adopts `Overflow.buttonCaps.get(button)` before natural-width capture (forcing recapture if a cached width is `<=` the active cap) so a capped `tab.header.Button` reused in a new toolbar lifts its cap before measuring and clears it once room returns. `hasFrozenDragButton()` / `queueSortDragProjection` / `scheduleSortDragProjection` defer briefly while a tab button carries `wrapperStyle.position === 'absolute'` from a settling cross-zone drag snapshot, bounded by `maxSortDragFrozenRetries` (`5` × `10 ms`) so a leaked `position: absolute` residue can never wedge the strip.

`agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline unit + e2e ran` (`change-class: restoration`).

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium Neural Link E2E on `apps/workstation` + Playwright unit suite) → L3 required (AC-1, AC-2, AC-3). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | Red-first Neural Link E2E in `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL.spec.mjs` (`'a capped title in the right zone and in a 320-px popup clears its cap and ellipsis within one projection when room returns (#20081)'`): pops out `commits` into a `320 × 240` window, verifies `neo-tab-overflow-capped` and `maxWidth < naturalWidth` (`224 < 263`), and proves single-projection (`whenProjectionIdle()`) restoration to `maxWidth: null` and no `neo-tab-overflow-capped` in both Arm 1 (popup widened by 200 px, `320 → 520 px`, including across a cross-toolbar move) and Arm 2 (focus moved so the focus-gated rail withdraws, `224 → 296 px` usable). Verified red on unpatched `dev` (`990669e521`) and green on `bc6fefe3dc`. |
| AC-2 | Unit arms in `test/playwright/unit/tab/plugin/Overflow.spec.mjs`: `'usable growth vs control: a usable that stays short keeps the cap and ledger; one that grows past natural width clears both (#20081)'`, `'cross-toolbar button move: a capped button moved to a wider toolbar lifts its cap before natural-width capture and clears (#20081)'`, `'cross-toolbar move to a second narrow strip: old plugin applySplit and destroy preserve the new strip cap and ellipsis class (#20081)'`, `'a leftover position:absolute residue caps its deferral retries and completes projection instead of wedging the strip (#20081)'`, and `'focus-gated rail reveal and withdraw re-projects Overflow so a focus-capped tab restores when focus leaves (#20081)'`. |
| AC-3 | Measured in `WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL.spec.mjs` (`lines 293-335`): in the 14%-extent `right-top-tabs` zone (`~185 px` wide), `Metrics` (`naturalWidth ≈ 62 px`) is genuinely capped (`maxWidth: 52`, `neo-tab-overflow-capped`) **while `right-top-tabs` holds focus** because the 5 focus-gated actions + overflow control occupy `~133 px` (`185 - 133 = 52 px` usable `< 62 px`), and was remaining capped as stale residue after focus left `right-top-tabs` (`~151 px` usable with only the `34 px` overflow control visible). With this fix, `Metrics` stays capped while `right-top-tabs` is focused and clears `neo-tab-overflow-capped` + restores `maxWidth: null` within one projection as soon as focus moves to `scale-tabs`. |
| AC-4 | Verified in the live multi-window Chromium popup sequence (`WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL.spec.mjs`); ready for operator repeat on the merged `dev` head. |

## Deltas from ticket
- In addition to firing `actionGeometryChange` (`{contextual: true}`) on focus-gated rail reveal/withdraw, traced the popup `Commits` `maxWidth: 61` residue to cross-toolbar button reuse (`Reconciler.reconcileTabChrome` moving a capped `tab.header.Button` into a new toolbar whose `Overflow` plugin had an empty `appliedCaps` Map, causing `project(true)` to measure `61 px` through the un-lifted cap and cache `naturalWidths[id] = 61`). Fixed via `Overflow.buttonCaps` (static `WeakMap`), `Overflow#releaseDepartedCap`, and bounded `hasFrozenDragButton()` deferral (`maxSortDragFrozenRetries = 5`).

### 📋 Required Actions

To proceed with merging, please address the following:

- [ ] **RA-1:** Move the cap's provenance off the `tab.header.Button` instance.
  - `button._overflowCap` is undeclared state that `Overflow` writes onto another class's instances. Any strip's plugin then reads it, and any of them may clear it, which is core-idiom check 5: one owner ends a lifetime.
  - Keep it in an `Overflow`-owned, class-level ledger instead, for example a `static` `WeakMap` keyed by the button. Every strip's plugin shares it in the one App worker, and it adds nothing to the Button's shape.
  - Alternatively, declare a documented member on `tab.header.Button`, if the Button should own it.
- [ ] **RA-2:** Make `destroy` release caps under the same ownership rule as `applySplit`.
  - `applySplit`'s departed branch skips a button that now sits in another overflow strip: `!departed.up?.('toolbar')?.getPlugin?.('tab-overflow')`.
  - `destroy` resolves `getTabButtons().find(…) || Neo.getComponent(buttonId)` and restores unconditionally.
  - Failure: a capped button moves to a popup strip, which adopts its cap. The old strip's plugin is destroyed (a dock rebuild) before its next `applySplit`. It removes `neo-tab-overflow-capped` and restores `maxWidth` on a button whose cap the new plugin still records.
  - The new plugin's next capped pass then takes the `appliedCaps.has` branch, which writes `maxWidth` back but never re-adds the class, leaving a cut title without its ellipsis.
  - Please share one guard (or helper) between both release paths, and add a unit arm: move a capped button, destroy the old plugin, and assert the new strip's cap keeps its class.
- [ ] **RA-3:** Bound the frozen-button deferral and give it an arm.
  - At `a9a3e9eef3`, `scheduleSortDragProjection` re-schedules every 10 ms while any tab button's `wrapperStyle.position === 'absolute'`.
  - Unlike the existing conditions (`sortSnapshotPending`, `startIndex`, `dragEndActive`), which the SortZone's own drag lifecycle clears, nothing owns clearing this style probe.
  - A leftover `position: absolute` therefore stops that strip's projection for good and keeps a 10-ms timer running. That residue class has been seen live before: on 2026-10-07 a returned tab kept its drag `wrapperStyle`.
  - Please tie the deferral to the drag that set it (for example the source SortZone's `dragEnd`), or cap its retries. Add a unit arm for the deferral and for its release, including the leftover-style case.
